newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah firms in slow late trading.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah firms in slow late trading.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah firmed against the dollar in late trading on Tuesday, with further uptrend seen likely following the elections, dealers said.

They said sentiment on the rupiah improved further after liquidity turned tighter in the afternoon. Offshore players were putting pressure on the dollar this morning but local purchases supported the downside on ample rupiah supply.
The relatively tight money market, probably due to higher weekly tax payments, drove the rupiah past the 2,429 resistance level and kept it trading at 2,428/29 at 0850 GMT.
Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,428.4/28.9 and 2,429.75/30.25 respectively.
Overnight rupiah rose to a high of 15.0 percent before settling at around 12.0 percent. It opened at eight percent.
Short-dated swaps were firmer following a tighter rupiah market, with overnight swaps traded at 0.05/0.10 and tom/next at 0.05/0.15 points.
One European bank dealer said operators were worried of a tight market after some state banks were seen desperately looking for rupiah supply since morning.
He said the market also focused on June 10, which was speculated to have a relatively high tax payment schedule.
"I suspect some operators took profits and established some outright positions," the dealer said.

He said the rupiah could sustain its uptrend as offshore operators seemed to start feeling comfortable with the election results despite an impending decision by the Moslem-based United Development Party (PPP) on acceptance of the outcome. The PPP had claimed widespread election irregularities.

The ruling Golkar swept more than 74 percent of the votes counted, with the PPP taking nearly 23 percent. Operators were worried of fresh violence and the immediate implication on the rupiah if the PPP declined to accept the election results.
Dealers said turnaround in the short term caused longer-term swap rates to climb after softening over the past few days.
One-month swaps edged up to 12.25/13.25 from 11.5/13.5, two to 25.0/26.0 from 24.0/25.0, three to 37.5/38.5 from 35.5/36.5 and six to 75.0/76.0 from 72.25/74.00 points.
The central bank raised its intervention band by one point to 2,418/2,610 and its conversion band also by one point to 2,418/2,466 on Tuesday.
